online_exposures: social media use (review's term; every pooled exposure instrument was a problematic or addictive social media use scale: BSMAS, SNAS, SMARS, PSMU)
population_notes: Adolescents and young adults (no combined category available): community, school and university samples; clinical inpatient psychiatric samples and children under 10 excluded; no upper age limit (deviation D1 from the registered 10 to 19 years); mean sample ages 15.60 to 21.47. Countries: USA, China, Hong Kong, Turkey, Lithuania, Germany. No samples from Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, or South/Southeast Asia despite 'Global' in the title.
last_search_date: April 2021 (end of publication-date limit 2010/01/01 to 2021/04/30; the date the searches were run is not reported)
primary_designs: 12 cross-sectional (all pooled studies; no longitudinal study or RCT contributed)

narrative_summary: All 12 pooled samples were cross-sectional and all exposures were problematic-use scales. Study-level r ranged 0.030 to 0.396 for depression (10 studies) and 0.220 to 0.580 for anxiety (7). In the 5 samples with both outcomes, associations did not differ (mean Fisher z difference −0.007, p = .77). Mean age explained nearly all depression heterogeneity.
narrative_locator: Results, 'Comparison Between Outcomes'. Quote: "The mean difference was −0.007 (t(4) = −0.32, p = .77; Wilcoxon signed-rank p = .88)"
author_conclusion: Social media use is positively associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents and young adults (small-to-moderate, no difference between outcomes); anxiety prediction interval includes zero, depression association weaker in adolescent samples, and cross-sectional evidence precludes causal inference.
rob_tool_used: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale adapted for cross-sectional designs (NOS-CS, 10 points); standard NOS cohort version for longitudinal studies (none in the pool); RoB 2 planned for RCTs but not applied (deviation D3). Study-level scores are said to be in Supplementary Table S2, which is not in the supplementary file.

noncritical_weaknesses: 3: N, eligible designs listed (cross-sectional, cohort, RCT) but no rationale given for the choice
6: PY, one extractor with independent verification by a second, but two pooled entries are labelled 'source unverified' in Tables 5a/5b
8: PY, tables give country, design, n, mean age, exposure and outcome instruments, r; no per-study recruitment setting or sex composition
10: N, funding sources of included studies not reported
12: N, low-risk-of-bias sensitivity analysis and NOS meta-regression are deferred to Supplementary Table S2, which is absent from the supplementary file; Table 3 says NOS scores are not yet finalised
amstar2.notes: Item 2 Y: PROSPERO CRD42024421214, deviations D1 to D7 tabulated with justifications (Table 7). Item 4 PY under the project rule: four databases with full strings (S1), Google Scholar first 200, citation chaining of four anchor reviews; no expert contact; English-only and peer-reviewed-only limits not justified; S1 'Records retrieved' yields never filled in. Under Shea et al.'s own PY criteria the unjustified language restriction would make item 4 N (critical flaw, overall Low). Item 7 PY: the three full-text exclusions are itemized with reasons in Table 4, but the PRISMA counts are an unfilled placeholder and Table 4 covers only studies 'for which a study-level record is held', so completeness cannot be confirmed. Item 9 PY: NOS-CS named and suited to the designs and weaknesses summarized across studies, but no study-level results are reported (S2 missing) and Table 3 says scores are not finalised; if the lead reviewer treats this as no completed assessment, item 9 becomes N (critical flaw; with item 4 also N, overall Critically low). Item 11 Y: Fisher z, DerSimonian-Laird random effects, Q, I², tau², prediction intervals, crude estimates not mixed with adjusted. Item 13 Y: discussion addresses self-report shared method variance, convenience university samples, cross-sectional design. Item 15 Y: Egger and trim-and-fill, low power discussed (contour-enhanced funnel plots referenced but absent from the supplement).

conflicts: No conflict of interest (as reported). Authors disclose generative AI use for language refinement only.
extraction_notes: (1) Table reconstruction: Tables 4, 5a, 5b, 6 and 7 printed out of order from the two-column PDF. I rebuilt rows from column order and checked them: per-study n sums to 5,774 (5a) and 5,286 (5b); the five within-study Fisher z differences reported in the text match the rebuilt r pairs (e.g. Wong et al. depression r 0.336 vs anxiety 0.384; Brailovskaia DE depression 0.396 vs anxiety 0.411; Kılınçel & Muratdağı anxiety 0.417); the mean-age-below-19 pools match the rebuilt ages (depression k = 4, N = 1,662; anxiety k = 3, N = 1,978). Table 6 rebuilt columns: Pooled r, 95% CI, 95% PI, I², Q (p), tau², Egger p. (2) Published Results contain an unfilled placeholder: '[Per-database yields and stage-by-stage counts to be inserted from the search and screening records, together with the corresponding PRISMA 2020 diagram.]' Records identified and screened are not reported; Figure 1 starts at eligibility (15 eligible, 3 excluded at full text, 12 pooled, 5 in both). (3) The supplementary file holds only Table S1, whose 'Records retrieved' column is not completed and which keeps a 'Note to author team' saying yields must be filled in from logs or by re-running the strings. Supplementary Table S2 (study-level NOS scores, low-risk sensitivity analysis, NOS meta-regression), Supplementary File S3 (R script), and the contour-enhanced funnel plots are cited but absent. (4) Two pooled entries are labelled 'source unverified': Kircaburun & Griffiths (2020) (depression r 0.340) and Brailovskaia et al. [LT] (depression 0.305, anxiety 0.246), contradicting the claim that every contributing estimate was verified against its source record. (5) The anxiety section says k = 7 'following the removal of the two entries described above', but no such entries are described earlier. (6) Methods say adjusted-only studies were 'retained for narrative synthesis', but deviation D7 says no narrative synthesis was conducted. (7) Record and citation title read 'A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis'; article heading reads 'A Meta-Analysis of Systematically Searched Evidence'; D7 says the title was changed to match. (8) Search publication-date limits end April 2021, yet citation chaining uses anchor reviews dated 2022 and 2024; PROSPERO number CRD42024... is described as registered in advance; search execution date not reported; evidence is over five years old at publication. (9) Cohen's kappa said to be computed at both stages but values not reported. (10) Eligibility allowed any social media use measure, but every pooled exposure is a problematic/addictive-use scale; the planned general vs problematic moderator was not tested. (11) Not recorded as findings: paired depression vs anxiety comparison (mean Fisher z difference −0.007, t(4) = −0.32, p = .77; Wilcoxon p = .88; invalid unpaired z = 1.71, p = .088); meta-regression of depression r on mean age (b = 0.045 per year, SE = 0.020, z = 2.27, p = .023; residual Q(8) = 4.24, p = .84), with no age gradient for anxiety; leave-one-out ranges (depression 0.247 to 0.289; anxiety 0.322 to 0.385); anxiety excluding Wong et al. r = 0.359 (95% CI 0.249 to 0.461; k = 6; N = 4,986; I² = 94.4%; PI −0.067 to 0.675). (12) Prediction intervals: depression 0.031 to 0.468; anxiety −0.009 to 0.646 (includes zero); depression mean age below 19 −0.370 to 0.656 (Table 6 only); anxiety mean age below 19 not reported (k = 3). tau²: 0.010, 0.020, 0.014, 0.030. Q: 55.82, 90.21, 20.76, 36.30 (all p < .001). (13) The age-restricted estimates are a sensitivity analysis (mean age below 19), recorded under the age-subgroup rule; no complementary estimate for older samples is reported. (14) Repeated mean ages worth checking against sources: Wang et al. and Kircaburun & Griffiths [33] both 16.29; Yıldız Durak and Kılınçel & Muratdağı both 15.60. (15) Outcomes outside the condition list: the registered secondary outcome psychological distress was not reported (D2); stress subscales were excluded from anxiety. (16) Combined unique participant total is not reported (depression N = 5,774 and anxiety N = 5,286 share five samples), so n_participants_total is null.
